title: The Raindrop Lie
hook: You have spent your entire life drawing the raindrop shape wrong.
script: You have spent your entire life drawing the raindrop shape wrong. We imagine a pointed tear, but nature doesn't work that way. What if you drew a raindrop the way it really falls? Tiny drops are actually near-perfect spheres. As they grow, air resistance pushes against the bottom. This dynamic pressure flattens the water into the shape of a hamburger bun. At 9 meters per second, they become liquid parachutes. Once they hit 6 millimeters, the air becomes so violent the drop simply disintegrates. The classic teardrop doesn't exist; it's flattened by the very air it falls through. Send this to the artist who still draws them as tears.

captions: The raindrop shape you've always drawn is a lie. Did you know this — yes or no?
Everything you know about rain is slightly wrong.
The physics of a falling drop is more unsettling than you think.
